_meta.fallback_method: WebSearch on ip.e-dunhuang.com and e-dunhuang.com cave-URI slugs (10.0001/0001.0001.NNNN); cross-referenced with UW Dunhuang Project public exhibitions for descriptions
_meta.platform_summary: Joint Dunhuang Academy × Tencent platform; world's first blockchain-tracked cultural-heritage co-creation library. Total inventory cited by official press: 448 murals + 9,409 materials + 697 scriptures across Mogao, Yulin, Maiji etc. License: personal / academic / appreciation free; commercial 300–800 RMB per image; on-chain authorization.
_meta.degradation_notes: Only cave-level metadata is extracted; per-mural / per-pattern IDs from the IP library would need direct site access. Image URLs deliberately empty — the platform's thumbnails are stable but were not retrievable from search snippets. License recorded as DunhuangFreeForResearch which matches the platform's posted terms for non-commercial use.

provenance_or_findsite: Mogao Grottoes, Dunhuang, Gansu province, China; middle section of the cliff
description: The earliest central-pillar (中心塔柱式) cave at Mogao. Square plan with a central pillar connecting the flat-ceiling rear to the floor; niches on all four sides of the pillar house statues. Wall paintings include the famous Northern Wei jataka scenes.

provenance_or_findsite: Mogao Grottoes, Dunhuang, Gansu province, China
description: Central-pillar cave from the first Mogao phase under the unified Northern Wei. West Wall of Main Chamber: upper register — sixteen heavenly musicians; middle — thousand-Buddhas with a central preaching scene; lower — Nine-coloured Deer (鹿王本生) jataka narrative.

provenance_or_findsite: Mogao Grottoes, Dunhuang, Gansu province, China
description: Contains a 'meditation Buddha' (禅定佛) of the Northern Wei period: 0.92 m tall, round-faced, seated cross-legged on a rectangular throne with hands in meditation mudra — a representative example of expressing the spirit through form (以形写神).

provenance_or_findsite: Mogao Grottoes, Dunhuang, Gansu province, China
description: Truncated-pyramid (覆斗顶) ceiling cave; one of the two most characteristic Western Wei caves at Mogao (with Cave 285). Ceiling combines Chinese mythological gods (Fuxi 伏羲, Nüwa 女媧, Lei Gong 雷公) with Indian Buddhist iconography — a key example of cross-cultural Western Wei painting.

provenance_or_findsite: Mogao Grottoes, Dunhuang, Gansu province, China
description: Western Wei Dynasty cave dated by an inscription to 538–539, also known as the 'Thousand Gods Palace'. Side-wall main subject is 'Five Hundred Robbers Becoming Buddhas' (五百强盗成佛). Walls combine Buddhist guardians (Cintamani, Lishi, apsaras) with traditional Chinese mythological deities (Lei Gong, Fuxi, Nüwa) — the most iconic syncretic cave at Mogao. Display style follows the so-called 'delicate-bone clear-image' (秀骨清像) aesthetic.

provenance_or_findsite: Mogao Grottoes, Dunhuang, Gansu province, China
description: Among the earliest Mogao caves (with Caves 267–271 and 275), tentatively dated to the Northern Liang period by the Dunhuang Research Academy. Features meditation-monk statues in niches on both sides of the outer gate entrance.

title_en: Digital Dunhuang Open Materials Library — license policy
date_raw: platform launched Dec 2022; major update Sep 2024
description: Pricing: per-image commercial license 300–800 RMB; personal appreciation / academic research / news reporting free download (resolution-tiered). Authorization is blockchain-recorded (on-chain materials, authorization, payment, download). Inventory (as of 2024 press release): 448 murals + 9,409 material units + 697 scriptures from Mogao, Yulin, Maiji and 6 other heritage sites.
